title: a-seal-fingerprints-the-import-closure-not-the-directory
intention: A validation seal's source_fingerprint covers the proof file plus the component files that proof actually imported, so an edit expires only the seals that load the edited file.
why: Measured 2026-09-05: one edit to transitions.py expired 30 tools/base proofs, 60 of 154 seals at once. Today (2026-09-07) clearing the inbox meant re-sealing 18 proofs whose code never changed — only a neighbour in the same directory did. The lived symptom is a wall of red that says nothing about what broke and an hour of re-seals to find out.
how: The tester already runs each proof in a subprocess; at exit the runner reports the subset of sys.modules whose __file__ is under the cairn repo (the import closure). validation_store.source_fingerprint hashes that file set plus the proof, sorted, and the seal records the set under evidence.fingerprint_closure beside the hash. build_inspector.component_color recomputes from the recorded closure instead of _source_fingerprint(comp_dir), so tester and inspector cannot disagree. The record says 'import closure' in words: a proof that open()s a file without importing it is a known hole, stated, not hidden.
falsifier: DONE when: (1) seal a proof under tools/base, edit a tools/base file that proof does not import, run the inspector — that seal still reads green while a proof importing the edited file reads expired; (2) evidence.fingerprint_closure lists only repo files and includes the proof; (3) the 2026-09-05 measurement re-run (touch transitions.py) expires only proofs that import transitions — count recorded in the ticket's crossings. WRONG INTENT if closure capture costs more than the copy it saves (measure seal wall-clock before/after).
traces_to: Law 3 — the horizon wording already says 'the code it proves'; hashing the directory measures something else. Law 1 — 18 needless re-seals today are the resolver re-deriving the settled. Residue of ticket 1b6516f92db3 (green-is-earned-not-assumed): 'yellow (dependency-change-only) is not yet derived — all changes read as red'; this is the deterministic form of yellow.
